jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Premium Parenting
jokes.joke: I once babysat on a cross-country flight because the parents upgraded themselves to first class and left me in coach with their five-year-old. During turbulence he asked, “Are we going to die?” I said, “Relax—your parents paid extra not to know.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Nap Time Bounty
jokes.joke: I babysit my nephew for extra cash, but I run it like a bounty hunter. I don't say 'bedtime,' I say 'target's last known location: the couch.' Kid negotiates like a hostage. 'Ten more minutes or I tell Mom you were on your phone.' "Fine," I say. "Twenty bucks, dead or asleep." Last week he escaped through the doggy door. I don't do this for the money anymore. I do it for the thrill of the chase.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Water Landings
jokes.joke: I love how calm flight attendants are when explaining how to survive plummeting from the sky. If I woke up to a house fire, I wouldn't calmly point out the nearest exits with two fingers. I'd be screaming in my underwear. But on an airplane, imminent death is just a mild inconvenience. 'In the event of a water landing...' Lady, we're flying over landlocked Ohio. If we hit water, that's not a landing, it's a geographical anomaly.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Bounty Babysitter
jokes.joke: You know, I used to be a babysitter, but I switched careers to bounty hunting. Turns out they're pretty much the same job. You're always tracking down someone who's trying to get away, they throw massive tantrums when you catch them, and at the end of the night you just want your money so you can go home and drink. The difference is, with bounty hunters, I don't have to sing lullabies to get them to sleep.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Airport Shift
jokes.joke: I once babysat a toddler at the airport, which is funny because I can barely manage my own emotions in public. He kept sprinting toward random gates like he had elite status. By the time we boarded, he’d convinced a stranger to trade seats so he could have the window, leaving me in the middle row holding his juice box like a defeated flight attendant.
